Q3901.t: A small island capital under a huge volcano
Q3901.s: Turquoise water laps the dark lava shores of Grande Comore, the largest island of the Comoros, and Moroni is built right on its west coast. Behind it the land climbs to Karthala, a broad active volcano topped by one of the largest summit craters in the world. The old town's narrow lanes and harbourside mosques recall centuries of Swahili and Arab trade across the Indian Ocean.
Q3901.w: A small city on a dark volcanic coast, with the long slopes of a huge volcano rising behind it.
f: Karthala rises to about 2,360 metres.
The Comoros are among the world's main producers of ylang-ylang, a flower oil used in perfume.
Coelacanths, the 'living fossil' fish, live in deep water off Grande Comore.

q.q: Which volcano towers over Moroni?

Q1025649.t: Vineyards in a valley ringed by high peaks
Q1025649.s: Neat green rows of vineyards and orchards turn the broad Breede River valley around Worcester into a patchwork. High, rugged mountains rise all around; the peaks of the Hex River range to the north-east are often white with snow in winter. The town was founded in 1820 and named after the Marquess of Worcester, brother of the Cape's governor, Lord Charles Somerset.
Q1025649.w: A town in a wide, flat valley of vineyards in neat rows, surrounded by high, rugged mountains.
f: The Worcester area is one of South Africa's largest wine-growing districts by volume.
The Karoo Desert National Botanical Garden, on the edge of town, shows plants of the arid interior.

q.q: Which river valley is Worcester in?

Q621001.t: Plateau town near giant falls and a rare antelope
Q621001.s: At about 1,150 metres, on a high, grassy plateau in northern Angola, Malanje looks out over savanna and farmland. North-west of the town, the Lucala River thunders over the Kalandula Falls, more than 100 metres high and among the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume. To the south-east, Cangandala National Park protects the giant sable antelope, Angola's national symbol.
Q621001.w: A town on a high, open plateau of grassland and fields, with river valleys cutting into it to the north-west.
f: To the west, the Black Rocks of Pungo Andongo, huge dark boulders, rise from the savanna.
The giant sable antelope, with long, sweeping horns, lives only in Angola.

q.q: Which rare antelope, Angola's national symbol, lives near Malanje?

Q122044.t: On the brink of a kilometre-high escarpment
Q122044.s: At about 1,760 metres on the Huíla plateau, Lubango is cooler and greener than the desert coast below. Just outside the city the plateau ends abruptly: at the Tundavala Gap the land drops away more than a kilometre to the plains, and at the Serra da Leba a famous road coils down the cliffs in tight hairpins towards the Namib and the Atlantic.
Q122044.w: A city on a high green plateau that ends in a sheer escarpment to the west, above dry lowlands.
f: Settlers from Madeira founded the modern town in the 1880s.
Lubango is the capital of Huíla province.

q.q: What was Lubango called in colonial times?

Q333476.t: The Bambara kings' capital on the Niger
Q333476.s: The Niger runs wide and slow past Ségou, its bank lined with mud-brick houses, fishing boats and fields. In the 18th and 19th centuries this was the capital of the Bambara Empire, which ruled the middle Niger. The town is famed for its shady balanzan trees, which drop their leaves in the rainy season and turn green in the dry one, the reverse of most trees.
Q333476.w: A town on the south bank of a very wide, slow river, amid flat farmland dotted with trees.
f: Downstream, the Markala dam feeds the huge Office du Niger irrigation scheme.
From here the Niger flows north-east towards Timbuktu and the edge of the Sahara.

q.q: Which empire had its capital at Ségou?

Q736061.t: Three rivers tangled in brown water and sandbars
Q736061.s: Bandundu sits on the east bank of the Kwango, just below the point where the Kwilu flows in, and only about 8 km before the Kwango itself empties into the Kasai. From above, the three rivers make a tangle of brown water, sandbars and green islands in a mosaic of forest and savanna. Boats between Kinshasa and Kikwit have long called here.
Q736061.w: A town on a broad brown river near two confluences, among sandbars, islands and a mix of forest and savanna.
f: In colonial times the town was called Banningville.
Bandundu is the capital of Kwilu province.

q.q: Which river does the Kwango join just below Bandundu?

Q188904.t: The Songhai capital at the great bend of the Niger
Q188904.s: Gao lies on the Niger where the river, having swung north into the Sahara, curves back towards the south-east. Across the water rise pale, pinkish dunes; on the town's side, fields and gardens hug the banks. Five centuries ago this was the capital of the Songhai Empire, one of the largest states in African history, and the mud-brick tomb of its ruler Askia Mohammed still stands.
Q188904.w: A town on a wide river curving through the desert, with pale dunes on the opposite bank.
f: The Tomb of Askia, a pyramid-shaped mud tower built in 1495, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The dune facing the town across the river is known as the Pink Dune.

q.q: Which empire made Gao its capital?

Q877122.t: Flat-topped hills and herds at a Sahel crossroads
Q877122.s: Around Tahoua the land breaks into the flat-topped hills and low mesas of the Ader, their dark caps of rock standing above sandy valleys. After the summer rains, ponds fill the hollows and millet fields turn green, before the long dry season bleaches everything to beige. Tahoua is one of Niger's main livestock markets, where herders from the north meet farmers from the south.
Q877122.w: A town among flat-topped hills and mesas, with sandy valleys and seasonal ponds between them.
f: Tahoua is the capital of one of Niger's regions, also called Tahoua.
Niger's capital, Niamey, lies nearly 400 km to the south-west.

q.q: Tahoua lies in which Sahel region of flat-topped hills?

Q824043.t: The Tropic of Capricorn, spiny forest and a reef
Q824043.s: The Tropic of Capricorn passes just south of Toliara, and the land here is Madagascar at its driest: spiny forest of strange, cactus-like plants, pale sand and brown riverbeds. Offshore, a great barrier reef runs along the coast, its line of white surf enclosing a turquoise lagoon. Fishing villages of the Vezo, a people of seafaring nomads, dot the shore.
Q824043.w: A town on a dry coast with a turquoise lagoon enclosed by a white line of reef, and pale scrubland inland.
f: Most plants of the spiny forest grow nowhere else on Earth.
The Onilahy River reaches the sea south of the town.

q.q: Which line of latitude passes just south of Toliara?

Q874317.t: An old trading town on the Milo River
Q874317.s: The Milo, a tributary of the Niger, winds through the flat, wooded savanna of Upper Guinea, and Kankan spreads along its banks. For centuries it was a crossroads for Malinke traders and a renowned centre of Islamic learning. The Fouta Djallon highlands lie far to the west; here the land is open and gently rolling, green after the rains and dusty gold in the dry season.
Q874317.w: A town on a winding river across flat, wooded savanna, green in the rainy season and golden in the dry.
f: Kankan is the capital of one of Guinea's regions, also called Kankan.
A railway more than 600 km long once linked Kankan with Conakry on the coast.

q.q: Which river flows past Kankan?

Q1947.t: Rocky hills and green islands on the White Nile
Q1947.s: The White Nile runs broad and braided past Juba, split by green islands and sandbars, while isolated rocky hills rise from the plain around the city. Downstream, the river disappears into the vast swamps of the Sudd. Nearby Gondokoro was a famous trading post, where in 1863 Speke and Grant, heading north from Lake Victoria, met Samuel and Florence Baker.
Q1947.w: A city on a wide, braided river with islands and sandbars, among scattered rocky hills.
f: Jebel Kujur, a rocky hill on the city's western edge, is a local landmark.
This stretch of the White Nile is often called the Bahr al-Jabal, 'river of the mountain'.

q.q: Which river flows past Juba?

Q498048.t: One of the world's great natural bays
Q498048.s: A huge, almost enclosed bay, often counted among the largest natural bays in the world, opens on Mozambique's far northern coast, and Pemba sits on a peninsula at its mouth. On the ocean side, white beaches and coral reefs fringe turquoise water. North of the town, the coral islands of the Quirimbas Archipelago string out along the coast.
Q498048.w: A town on a peninsula beside a vast, almost enclosed bay, with white beaches and turquoise reefs on the ocean side.
f: Pemba is the capital of Cabo Delgado province.
Quirimbas National Park protects islands, reefs and mangroves north of the town.

q.q: What was Pemba called in colonial times?

Q502216.t: Pine plantations above, Lake Malawi below
Q502216.s: Huge pine plantations spread in dark-green blocks across the Viphya Plateau, and Mzuzu lies at its northern edge, in the hills of northern Malawi. Coffee grows on the surrounding slopes. About 40 km to the east, the land falls steeply to Lake Malawi, a long blue lake filling a section of the Great Rift Valley.
Q502216.w: A town in green hills, with dark blocks of pine forest to the south and a steep drop to a long lake to the east.
f: The Viphya pine plantations are among the largest planted forests in Africa.
Lake Malawi is about 580 km long.

q.q: Which lake lies about 40 km east of Mzuzu?

Q738496.t: A Red Sea port near the Bab-el-Mandeb
Q738496.s: Assab lies on the scorching Danakil coast, one of the hottest inhabited places on Earth, where black lava and pale sand meet the Red Sea. About 80 km to the south-east the sea narrows into the Bab-el-Mandeb strait. In 1869 an Italian shipping company bought land on this bay, the first foothold of what later became the Italian colony of Eritrea.
Q738496.w: A small port on a flat, sun-scorched coast of dark lava and pale sand, near the Red Sea's southern outlet.
f: Summer temperatures here often exceed 40°C.
Inland, parts of the Danakil Depression lie more than 100 metres below sea level.

q.q: Which strait lies about 80 km south-east of Assab?

Q332319.t: Highland city at the end of the salt caravans
Q332319.s: High on the Tigray highlands, at over 2,000 metres, Mekele is ringed by stony plateaus and terraced fields. For centuries camel caravans climbed up here from the Danakil Depression, one of the lowest and hottest places on Earth, carrying bars of rock salt cut from its white salt flats. In the 1880s Emperor Yohannes IV made the town his seat and built a palace.
Q332319.w: A city on a high, stony plateau of terraced fields; to the east the land plunges towards a deep, pale desert.
f: The salt bars, called amole, were once used as money in Ethiopia.
Parts of the Danakil Depression lie more than 100 metres below sea level.

q.q: What have camel caravans long carried up to Mekele?

Q3904.t: Next door to one of the world's biggest granite domes
Q3904.s: Mbabane climbs the green hills of the Mdimba range in Eswatini's highveld, at about 1,200 metres. Just north of the city rises Sibebe, a vast bare dome of granite often described as one of the largest in the world, its smooth grey flanks shining after rain. South of town, the Ezulwini Valley, the 'Valley of Heaven', runs down towards the royal village of Lobamba.
Q3904.w: A city on steep green hills, with a huge bare grey dome of rock to the north and a broad valley to the south.
f: Sibebe rises to about 1,490 metres.
Highland Mbabane is cooler and wetter than the lowveld to the east.

q.q: What is Sibebe, near Mbabane?

Q165422.t: Botswana's gold-rush town on the Tati River
Q165422.s: In 1869 the Tati area set off one of the earliest gold rushes in southern Africa, and Francistown grew from that mining camp into Botswana's second city. It spreads over flat, dry bushveld along the sandy bed of the Tati River, which runs only after rain. The border with Zimbabwe is less than 100 km away, and the main railway north runs through the town.
Q165422.w: A town on flat, dry bushveld along a sandy riverbed, with a railway running north to south through it.
f: The town is named after Daniel Francis, a mining pioneer of the 1890s.
Francistown lies at about 1,000 metres above sea level.

q.q: What first drew prospectors to the Francistown area in 1869?

Q910616.t: A cocoa town in Cameroon's southern rainforest
Q910616.s: Deep in the rainforest of southern Cameroon, about 115 km south of Yaoundé, the forest around Ebolowa is patched with cocoa farms and plantain gardens on gently rolling land. A small lake sits right in the centre of town. It is the capital of Cameroon's South Region, which stretches to the borders of Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.
Q910616.w: A town in rolling, dark-green rainforest, with a small lake at its centre and farms patched into the forest around it.
f: Cocoa, grown in the shade of forest trees, is the main cash crop here.
There are two rainy seasons a year, typical of an equatorial climate.

q.q: Which crop is the mainstay of farms around Ebolowa?

Q184184.t: Iron-ore trains and monk seals on a desert peninsula
Q184184.s: Nouadhibou lies on a long, narrow peninsula of sand and rock pointing south into the Atlantic, split lengthwise by a border. Iron-ore trains, among the longest and heaviest in the world, rumble some 700 km across the Sahara from Zouérat to the port here. At the peninsula's tip, Cap Blanc shelters the largest surviving colony of Mediterranean monk seals.
Q184184.w: A town on the east side of a long, narrow desert peninsula, facing a sheltered bay; a railway comes in from the east.
f: For years the bay was a graveyard for hundreds of abandoned ships.
The shallows of the Banc d'Arguin, to the south-east, are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

q.q: What do the long trains arriving at Nouadhibou carry?

Q218928.t: A vast bay at the northern tip of Madagascar
Q218928.s: Antsiranana wraps around one of the largest natural harbours in the world, a deep, many-armed bay almost cut off from the Indian Ocean by a narrow entrance. In the middle of the bay stands a small island shaped like a sugarloaf. To the south rises Montagne d'Ambre, a green volcanic massif whose rainforest stands out sharply against the dry lowlands around it.
Q218928.w: A town on a peninsula in a huge, many-armed bay with a narrow entrance, and a green mountain massif to the south.
f: Montagne d'Ambre National Park is home to lemurs and tiny chameleons.
Outside the bay's entrance lies a turquoise lagoon known as the Emerald Sea.

q.q: What was Antsiranana formerly called?

Q126124.t: Forested hills rising from Togo's coastal plain
Q126124.s: North of the coastal plain, the flat land gives way to forested hills at Atakpamé, the southern end of the mountain chain that runs diagonally across Togo into Benin and Ghana. The town spreads over several hills, with coffee and cocoa farms on the green slopes around it. It is the capital of Togo's Plateaux Region, about 160 km north of Lomé.
Q126124.w: A town spread over green, forested hills, at the southern end of a mountain chain running north-east.
f: To the north-east, the Togo Mountains continue into Benin as the Atakora range.
Coffee and cocoa are the main crops of the surrounding Plateaux Region.

q.q: Atakpamé lies at the southern end of which mountain chain?

Q325164.t: One of Africa's hottest towns, on the Senegal River
Q325164.s: Kayes lies on the Senegal River in western Mali, in a low basin ringed by flat-topped sandstone hills, and it is often called one of the hottest towns in Africa: in April and May, afternoons regularly top 40°C. Upstream, the river spills over rocky ledges at the Félou and Gouina falls. From the 1880s a railway was pushed from here towards the Niger.
Q325164.w: A town on a winding river in a hot, low basin ringed by flat-topped hills.
f: The old French fort of Médine, built in 1855, stands on the river just upstream.
Kayes is the capital of Mali's westernmost region.

q.q: Which river flows through Kayes?

Q575780.t: A green ribbon of vines across the Kalahari
Q575780.s: Around Upington the Kalahari is red sand and dry scrub, but the Orange River cuts through it with a startling green ribbon of vineyards, orchards and lucerne fields. Grapes grown here are dried in the sun to make raisins and sultanas. The town's airport has one of the longest runways in the world, about 4.9 km: heavy jets need a long run in the hot desert air.
Q575780.w: A town on a river lined with a sharp green strip of vineyards, cutting through red-brown semi-desert.
f: Augrabies Falls, where the Orange plunges into a granite gorge, lies about 90 km to the west.
Summer afternoons here often climb above 35°C.

q.q: Which river brings green fields to Upington?

Q587152.t: An ivory-era trading town near the Lualaba
Q587152.s: A short way east of the Lualaba, the great upper course of the Congo, Kasongo stands on a plateau of savanna and forest strips at about 670 metres. In the 1870s it became the headquarters of Tippu Tip, the most famous of the Swahili-Arab traders from Zanzibar, and grew to a town of some 20,000 people, a hub of the ivory and slave trade.
Q587152.w: A town on a plateau of savanna and dark strips of forest, a short way east of a broad river.
f: The Lualaba is the name given to the upper Congo River, above Kisangani.
Kasongo lies near the point where the Luama River joins the Lualaba.

q.q: Which famous trader made Kasongo his headquarters in the 1870s?

Q6271177.t: A sugar town in the green Niari valley
Q6271177.s: Just 2 km apart, on either side of the small Livouba River, Kayes and its larger twin Nkayi share the fertile Niari valley of the Republic of the Congo. From above the two read as one town, ringed by the geometric blocks of sugar-cane plantations that make this the country's sugar centre. The Congo–Ocean Railway, linking Pointe-Noire with Brazzaville, passes through Nkayi.
Q6271177.w: A small town merged with a larger one in a broad green valley, ringed by big rectangular cane fields.
f: Kayes is the capital of Kayes District in Bouenza department.
Nkayi was called Jacob until 1975, after a French railway engineer.

q.q: Which crop grows on the plantations around Kayes and Nkayi?

Q805946.t: Savanna and gallery forest on the Ouaka River
Q805946.s: Open savanna alternates with gallery forest along the streams in the rolling heart of the Central African Republic, and Bambari sits on the Ouaka River in the middle of it. After the rains the land is green to the horizon; in the dry season grass fires leave dark scars across it. The town is the capital of Ouaka prefecture and a crossroads of roads running east and north.
Q805946.w: A town on a winding river amid rolling savanna, with dark strips of forest along the valleys.
f: The Ouaka is a tributary of the Ubangi, which feeds the Congo.
The capital, Bangui, lies about 280 km to the south-west.

q.q: Which river flows past Bambari?

Q220843.t: Where giant dunes meet a flamingo lagoon
Q220843.s: At Walvis Bay the Namib's tall dunes run right down to the Atlantic, and a long sand spit, Pelican Point, curls around a sheltered bay. South of town a shallow lagoon turns pink with flocks of flamingos, and beyond it lie the white and pink rectangles of salt works. Cold sea fog is common, yet it hardly ever rains here.
Q220843.w: A town on a sheltered bay behind a long, hooked sand spit, with orange dunes and pink salt pans to the south.
f: The lagoon is a protected wetland and one of southern Africa's most important sites for coastal birds.
Walvis Bay is Namibia's main port.

q.q: What does the name Walvis Bay mean?

Q170724.t: Right on the Tropic of Capricorn, in the bushveld
Q170724.s: Mahalapye sits almost exactly on the Tropic of Capricorn, marked by a small monument beside the main highway. The town lies on the road and railway between Gaborone and Francistown, amid flat, dry bushveld of thorn trees and red sand. To the north-east rise the Tswapong Hills, which catch more rain than the plains and stay noticeably greener.
Q170724.w: A town on a straight railway and highway across flat, dry bushveld, with low hills to the north-east.
f: The Tswapong Hills rise about 400 metres above the surrounding plain.
On the Tropic of Capricorn the sun stands directly overhead at the December solstice.

q.q: Which two cities does the road through Mahalapye link?

Q855634.t: Royal village of the Bamangwato, around its hill
Q855634.s: A sprawling traditional village of homesteads and fields, Serowe spreads around a low, rocky hill on the edge of the Kalahari sandveld. In 1902 Khama III, chief of the Bamangwato, moved his capital here, and the royal graves lie on the hill. His grandson Seretse Khama, Botswana's first president, was born in Serowe in 1921.
Q855634.w: A large, spread-out village around a low rocky hill, where hills meet flat, sandy bush.
f: The Khama Rhino Sanctuary, north of Serowe, protects rhinos on the edge of the Kalahari.
Serowe is often described as one of the largest villages in Africa.

q.q: Who moved the Bamangwato capital to Serowe in 1902?

Q934149.t: A green town on Mount Kenya, right by the equator
Q934149.s: Meru lies on the north-eastern slopes of Mount Kenya, just north of the equator, in a lush belt of tea, coffee and banana gardens fed by mountain streams. Above it the forest climbs towards the mountain's jagged summit, flecked with the last of its glaciers. Eastwards the land drops into dry, hot bush, where Meru National Park became famous as the home of Elsa, the lioness of Born Free.
Q934149.w: A town on green, cultivated slopes below a high mountain, with dry plains falling away to the east.
f: Mount Kenya rises to 5,199 metres, the second-highest peak in Africa.
Joy Adamson released Elsa into the wild in Meru National Park.

q.q: On the slopes of which mountain does Meru stand?

Q3726.t: An island capital at the mouth of the Gambia River
Q3726.s: Banjul fills a small, low island where the Gambia River meets the Atlantic, its estuary several kilometres wide and fringed with mangroves. The British founded it in 1816 as Bathurst. Upstream, the river and the narrow country that follows its banks wind more than 300 km inland, like a long green finger pressed into Senegal.
Q3726.w: A small city on a low island at a wide, mangrove-fringed river mouth on the Atlantic coast.
f: Kunta Kinteh Island, upstream in the river, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa.

q.q: Which country almost surrounds The Gambia?

Q459369.t: A forest city near Earth's natural nuclear reactors
Q459369.s: In the hilly south-east of Gabon, rainforest gives way to the grassy Batéké Plateaux, and here, near the upper Ogooué, Franceville grew. The explorer Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza founded it in 1880 as a village for freed slaves. North-west of the city, at Oklo, uranium ore some two billion years ago sustained natural nuclear chain reactions, the only natural reactors known on Earth.
Q459369.w: A city among green hills where dense forest meets open, grassy plateaus.
f: The Oklo reactors switched on and off for hundreds of thousands of years.
Franceville is the capital of Haut-Ogooué province.

q.q: What happened naturally at Oklo, near Franceville?

Q134086.t: Green circles in the heart of the Libyan Desert
Q134086.s: Hundreds of kilometres from any other town, the Kufra oasis appears as a cluster of perfect green circles in an ocean of sand: fields watered by pivot sprinklers. Al Jawf is its main town. The water is fossil groundwater, stored in sandstone beneath the Sahara since wetter times thousands of years ago. In 1895 the Senussi order made remote Kufra its headquarters.
Q134086.w: A small town beside dozens of bright green circular fields, alone in a vast expanse of pale sand.
f: The green circles of Kufra are a classic sight in photographs taken from space.
The Nubian Sandstone Aquifer beneath Kufra is one of the largest stores of groundwater in the world.

q.q: What are the green circles around Kufra?

Q524984.t: Flood-fed fields where the Gorgol meets the Senegal
Q524984.s: The Gorgol flows in from the Mauritanian interior to meet the Senegal River at Kaédi, on its north bank. Each year the river floods its broad valley, and as the water recedes farmers sow sorghum in the damp soil, drawing a ribbon of green across the Sahel. The town's regional hospital, built of local brick under rows of domes, won an Aga Khan Award for Architecture.
Q524984.w: A town on a broad river valley of green fields in the Sahel, where a tributary joins from the north.
f: Across the river lies Senegal; the Senegal River forms the border here.
Kaédi is the capital of the Gorgol region.

q.q: Which river joins the Senegal at Kaédi?

Q1002188.t: A Karoo town halfway between two others
Q1002188.s: High, open plains of the Upper Karoo, at about 1,280 metres, stretch around Middelburg, with the Sneeuberg range rising to the south. It was founded in 1852 and named for lying midway between Graaff-Reinet and Colesberg. Around it stretches sheep country: brown plains studded with dark, flat-topped dolerite hills and dotted with windpumps and small dams.
Q1002188.w: A small town on wide, brown Karoo plains studded with dark, flat-topped hills, with mountains to the south.
f: The Sneeuberg, 'Snow Mountain', is often white with snow in winter.
Sheep farming, especially for Merino wool, has long been the area's main business.

q.q: Between which two towns is Middelburg roughly midway?

Q159325.t: A German-era harbour town on a bare desert coast
Q159325.s: Lüderitz huddles around a rocky bay on Namibia's southern coast, with nothing but the Namib behind it. Bartolomeu Dias set up a stone cross on the headland here in 1488. Four centuries later the town grew as a German trading post, and its colourful colonial houses still climb the granite. A few kilometres inland, the diamond town of Kolmanskop lies abandoned, its houses filling with sand.
Q159325.w: A small town on a rocky, indented bay of a bare desert coast, with dunes and gravel plains inland.
f: Diamonds were found near Kolmanskop in 1908, setting off a rush.
Much of the desert around Lüderitz was long a closed diamond area, the Sperrgebiet.

q.q: Which explorer raised a stone cross near Lüderitz in 1488?

Q2301363.t: Copper hills that burst into flower each spring
Q2301363.s: Bare granite domes surround Springbok in Namaqualand, a semi-desert of grey-brown scrub for most of the year. Then, after the winter rains, usually in August and September, the land can erupt in carpets of orange, white and purple daisies. Copper drew the first settlers: South Africa's first commercial mine opened near here in 1852.
Q2301363.w: A small town among bare, rounded granite hills in dry, grey-brown scrubland.
f: The town is named after the springbok, a gazelle that once roamed here in great herds.
Goegap Nature Reserve, just outside town, protects hundreds of species of flowering plants.

q.q: What transforms Namaqualand around Springbok in August and September?

Q101418.t: Eswatini's royal village in the Valley of Heaven
Q101418.s: Lobamba lies in the green Ezulwini Valley, the 'Valley of Heaven', between Mbabane and Manzini. It is Eswatini's royal and legislative capital, home to Parliament and the Queen Mother's royal residence. Each year tens of thousands of young women gather here for Umhlanga, the reed dance, carrying tall reeds to the royal village in a colourful procession.
Q101418.w: A small, spread-out settlement in a wide green valley between steep hills, along the road between two towns.
f: Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary, Eswatini's oldest protected area, borders the valley.
The National Museum of Eswatini is in Lobamba.

q.q: Which ceremony draws tens of thousands to Lobamba each year?

Q175596.t: On Mauritania's Road of Hope, where Sahara meets Sahel
Q175596.s: Ayoun el Atrous lies in south-eastern Mauritania, where the Sahara gives way to the Sahel: rocky outcrops, sandy plains and, after the summer rains, a thin green wash of grass and acacias. It is the capital of the Hodh El Gharbi region and a stop on the Road of Hope, the long highway that crosses the country from Nouakchott towards Néma.
Q175596.w: A town on a dry, sandy plain with rocky outcrops, along a single long highway running east to west.
f: The region's name, Hodh El Gharbi, means 'Western Basin'.
Almost all of the year's rain falls between July and September.

q.q: Ayoun el Atrous is the capital of which Mauritanian region?

Q614754.t: A remote desert well on the stony Sahara
Q614754.s: Bir Lehlou is a tiny settlement in the north-east of Western Sahara, close to the Mauritanian border, gathered around a well on a vast, stony plain. From above, the land here is a hamada of brown and grey gravel, crossed by shallow dry wadis and low rocky ridges. The name means 'the sweet well', a reminder of how precious fresh water is out here.
Q614754.w: A handful of buildings on a vast, flat plain of brown gravel crossed by faint dry riverbeds.
f: Smara, the nearest sizeable town, lies more than 200 km to the north-west.
Rain here is rare and irregular; in some years almost none falls.

q.q: What does the name Bir Lehlou mean?

Q4117083.t: A tiny palm oasis deep in the Fezzan
Q4117083.s: Tmassa is a small oasis in Libya's Fezzan, about 160 km south-east of Sabha: a patch of date palms and gardens around precious groundwater, with sand and stony desert in every direction. Only a few hundred people live here. Travellers heading east to the volcanic crater of Waw an Namus, with its coloured lakes, often pass through.
Q4117083.w: A small dark-green patch of palms in a huge expanse of pale sand and stony desert.
f: Waw an Namus is a volcanic caldera in the Sahara holding small lakes of strikingly different colours.
The Fezzan is the south-western of Libya's three historic regions.

q.q: In which historic region of Libya is Tmassa?
